title: Specified completed scalar Hom comparison via evaluation on arbitrary schemes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed algebraic closure, their valuation rings and uniformizers $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $W$ be any scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$ and $S=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $T=-\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}S$ be ordinary derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $C=C_{L/E}$ the specified strict-quotient-tower integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], and $H_R,H_S$ ambient derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Take $M,N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ such that $H_R(M,N)\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. For $Z=M,N,H_R(M,N)$ use precisely the quotient-augmentation comparison $\chi_Z:TZ\xrightarrow{\sim}CZ$ of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Let $\gamma_{M,N}:TH_R(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_S(TM,TN)$ be the ordinary evaluation-transpose map [lem-sf-ringed-finite-free-hom-base-change].

The specified Hom operation comparison $\theta^{\mathcal Hom}_{L/E;M,N}:CH_R(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_S(CM,CN)$ of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], used by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], satisfies the equality of actual derived morphisms
$$\theta^{\mathcal Hom}_{L/E;M,N}\circ\chi_{H_R(M,N)}=H_S(\chi_M^{-1},\chi_N)\circ\gamma_{M,N}.$$
Here specified means the following chain-Hom construction, with its fixed localized resolution augmentations, not an arbitrary natural isomorphism with tower laws. Choose a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to M$, a K-injective representative $I$ of $N$, and a flat-term K-flat resolution $q:Q\to\mathcal Hom_R^\bullet(P,I)$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. With the fixed augmentation $j:I\otimes_RS\to J=I_S(I\otimes_RS)$, its ordinary chain map is
$$Q\otimes_RS\longrightarrow\mathcal Hom_S^\bullet(P\otimes_RS,J),\qquad x\otimes s\longmapsto\bigl(m\otimes b\longmapsto j(q(x)(m)\otimes sb)\bigr).$$
It is followed and conjugated by precisely the input and output quotient completion maps $\chi$, including their zero shifted-product coordinates. Hom differential and evaluation use [def-pur-hom-complex, def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model, def-coef-hom-representative-evaluation]. This construction is independent of representatives through the canonical localized resolution comparisons and equals the specified operation comparison. Equivalently, after $\chi$ identifications its tensor-Hom transpose is $TM\otimes_S^{\mathbf L}TH_R(M,N)\cong T(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}H_R(M,N))\xrightarrow{T(\operatorname{ev})}TN$.

proof.text: Unfold the existing specified comparison scalarHomCompleted of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension]. It is the composite of the inverse Hom-output completion comparison, the ordinary evaluation-transpose scalarHomOrdinary, and the internal-Hom image of the inverse first-input and direct second-input completion comparisons. The canonical scalarCompletionIso has scalarCompletion as its forward map. Cancel the Hom-output forward map with its inverse to obtain the first displayed equality, as an equality of actual morphisms.

proof.text: Further compose with the internal-Hom image of the direct first-input and inverse second-input comparisons. Functoriality on the product category and the two isomorphism cancellation equations reduce this composite to scalarHomOrdinary. By coefficientBaseChangeHom of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], scalarHomOrdinary is definitionally the closed transpose of the inverse ordinary tensor comparison followed by scalar-extended evaluation. Applying the inverse equivalence cancels the transpose, giving precisely the second displayed equality.

proof.text: For the chain clause, apply specifiedHomScalarChain of [lem-zl-specified-hom-scalar-evaluation] to the given P, I, Q and q. That declaration already has the same arbitrary-scheme hypotheses, fixed K-injective augmentations, sheaf-section formula and unique chain map; unlike the older finite-field evaluation theorem in its module, the chain declaration needs no finite-field structure on X. Apply the forward closed transpose to the second equality from the preceding step. Its application to the inverse transpose cancels, identifying the three-completion-map composite with scalarHomOrdinary. Reassociate and substitute this equality into the existing chain localization square. The section formula is unchanged. Conversely, substitute it into any candidate completed square and apply uniqueness in specifiedHomScalarChain. This proves existence and uniqueness with the prescribed completed comparison.
